newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Dollar boosts European bourses, gold slips.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Dollar boosts European bourses, gold slips.

text.p: The dollar surged to a near two-year high against the mark on Tuesday, powering German shares to a record high and French stocks within sight of historic levels.
British stocks also overcame some of their interest rate jitters to recoup Monday's fall, helped by a strong bond market and Wall Street's late rally overnight to close flat.
Gold was back in the doldrums, fixing in London at $369.00 an ounce, its lowest fix in three years and after taking another beating overnight.
Analysts forecast gold would weaken further as a strong dollar discouraged buyers and selling by gold mining houses cast a bearish pall over the market.

The dollar shot to 23-month highs against the mark, French franc and Swiss franc in overnight dealings after comments by German and U.S. officials on the dollar's status as a reserve currency ahead of European monetary and economic union (EMU).
Foreign exchange markets were galvanised by Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing saying on Monday that investors might want to switch into dollars in the runup to EMU in 1999.

"The general trend of the dollar continuing to strengthen is in place...But we are going to have some further hiccups on the road to monetary union and at those times we may see the deutschemark strengthen," said David Brickman, European analyst at Yamaichi International.
The mark's softness against both the dollar and yen will please the French. They have argued for a dollar rise against the mark which would feed through into a more competitive franc.
Profit-taking knocked the dollar off its highs and by 1230 GMT, it was quoted at 1.5635 marks and 114.03 yen against 1.5428 marks and 113.68 yen in late Europe on Monday.
On European stock markets, Germany's 30-share DAX index stormed to a fresh record at the start of trade, boosted by the rise of the dollar which makes German exports more competitive.
The DAX started at a high of 2,892.57, then pared its gains to trade up 28 points at 2,886.

Shares of carmaker Volkswagen inched up about six marks to 593 after falling nearly five percent on Monday on worries about the company's legal dispute with General Motors over allegations of industrial espionage.
The dollar and strong bond markets were also behind a strong rally in French shares, which surged nearly 33 points, or 1.4 percent, to their best levels this year.
The CAC-40 index was trading only eight points below its record high of 2,360.98 set on February 2 1994.

The dollar was the main cause of the Bourse's rise, dealers said. Companies with U.S. units, heavy exports to the United States or those in competition with U.S. manufacturers were the biggest beneficiaries.
"The rise may look excessive but if you look at it objectively, Paris is lagging the other European markets, particularly Frankfurt, where the gap is 500 points," one trader said.
Renewed strength in government bonds, coupled with Wall Street's rebound, helped British shares recoup Monday's losses.

The blue-chip FTSE 100 index was up around 20 points at 4,059 by 1230 GMT. Its morning gains, lifted the FTSE back towards its intraday record of 4,094.4 set on November 26, with some traders saying it remained poised for a traditional year-end rally.
Trading volumes were thin, however, and worries remained about the strength of sterling and rising interest rates.

Sterling hit a high of 2.6370 marks in overnight trading -- its highest level since sterling dropped out of the European exchange rate mechanism in 1992. It later dropped back and was quoted at 2.6117 marks.
CURRENCIES AT 1230 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.5635 marks and 114.03 yen against 1.5428 marks and 113.68 yen in late Europe on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1230 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares was up 20.7 points, or 0.51 percent, at 4,059.2.
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index was up 34.10 points, or 1.47 percent, at 2,352.73.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 28.10 points, or 0.98 percent, at 2,886.70.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold fixed at $369.00 an ounce, down from $370.75 on Monday afternoon and its lowest level since November 2, 1993.
